work_order.understanding:
Three things must be separated: two belong to the built attempt, one is mine to fix.

FIRST — what the built attempt got wrong, which QA proved. canNarrowAxisByConditions reasons about the axis/query divergence along exactly ONE dimension: which FIELD a condition addresses. That question is necessary and not sufficient, and the missing half is that it silently assumes a disjunct addressed to the axis is also READ the same way by the axis and by the query. They are not. filterCategoriesByConditions (budgetDataQuery.ts:128-133) reads `contains` as textValue.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase()) — a literal substring test. conditionsToAQL (transaction-rules.ts:641-649) compiles the same condition to $like with pattern '%' + value + '%'; compiler.ts:733-736 emits UNICODE_LIKE(getNormalisedString(right), NORMALISE(left)); unicodeLike.ts:5-31 turns that into a JS regex in which '%' is '.*' and '?' is '.'. One side is a string search, the other a pattern language, and nothing escapes the user's value. So BUG-2 needs no 'any of' at all — a single `Category contains %` under 'all of' drops every cent — and BUG-3 is the same divergence reached under 'or'. Screening for the operator would have treated the symptom and left a legitimate filter permanently unable to narrow.

SECOND — a claim in my own previous revision that was WRONG, which I checked rather than shipped. It said the axis's `matches` branch is a money-losing third instance, because of its `condition.value.length <= 256` guard: over that length the axis 'rejects the value for every category'. I executed the served function itself and it does the opposite — the failed length test skips the `if` and control falls through to `return true`, keeping EVERY category, which is the safe direction. The other `matches` divergences are the same shape: the /i flag matches strictly more than the query's case-sensitive REGEXP. Not one `matches` value can lose money. The previous revision built AC-16 and two test cases on that; they assert a defect that does not exist and would fail against correct code. That criterion is withdrawn and `matches` is out of scope.

THIRD — the plan reviewer's objection to my previous revision, which is CORRECT and which I verified by execution before accepting. It said AC-14/AC-15 claim a filter whose value 'CONTAINS a SQL wildcard character' leaves the report exactly as an unfiltered one, and that this is false for every such value except the bare wildcard. It is false: value '%' and '?' each match 25 of 25 names, but 'o%' matches 7, 'Fo%' 1, '% Off' 1 — a value that merely embeds a wildcard is a perfectly good narrowing filter. That is the reviewer catching a criterion that contradicts the rule it is stated to express, which is the one case where rewriting the criterion is right. AC-14, AC-15 and AC-17 are rescoped: the bare wildcard is named as such, embedded values are governed by AC-17's one-directional superset property, and 'o%' passes. The objection lands in the criteria, the unit test, the e2e case and the qa_script step — all four, not just the quoted clause.

The mechanism is unchanged: make the axis evaluate the text operators through the same primitives the query uses, so the two agree by construction. AC-1..AC-13 carry forward unchanged and unrenumbered.
work_order.root_cause:
The report's row axis (narrowCategoriesByConditions in packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/budgetDataQuery.ts, called from custom-spreadsheet.ts:91-97 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:43-49) assumes the axis and the query select the same set for the same condition. For the id-valued operators that holds; for `contains` it does not, because the two sides implement it in different languages. The axis reads it as a literal substring test (budgetDataQuery.ts:128-130); the query compiles it to $like '%'+value+'%' (transaction-rules.ts:641-649) → UNICODE_LIKE(getNormalisedString(right), NORMALISE(left)) (compiler.ts:733-736) → a JS regex where '%' is '.*' and '?' is '.', with nothing escaping the user's value (unicodeLike.ts:5-31). They also fold differently: the axis lowercases both sides, the query folds case AND diacritics (getNormalisedString, shared/normalisation.ts:9-15).

Both consequences put the axis in a strict SUBSET of the query — the direction that silently discards money. (1) `Category contains %` (BUG-2): the axis keeps at most the categories whose name contains a literal percent sign while the query's '%%%' matches every name; executed over a ten-category fixture, axis 1 vs query 10. QA measured the consequence in the browser on six independent demo budgets: Split=Category rendered zero rows and 0.00 every time, while Split=Payee — same query, unnarrowed axis — reported the full baseline (-7163.13, -6081.81, -7618.39, -8760.30, -6853.97, -8802.21). (2) The same condition under 'any of' beside a second category disjunct (BUG-3): the gate returns true because both disjuncts are category fields, the axis narrows to the selected group, and the query's $or unions in a '%' arm matching everything, so 'Food' and all spending outside Bills is fetched then discarded. A third divergence of the same shape, found by execution and not reported: diacritic folding — `contains 'cafe'` keeps 0 on the axis and 1 ('Café') on the query.

What this is NOT, checked by executing the served code rather than reading it: `matches` diverges in the OPPOSITE and harmless direction. The /i flag makes the axis match strictly more than the query's case-sensitive REGEXP (value 'RE' keeps Rent and Restaurants against the query's zero), and the 256-character guard does not reject long values at all — the failed length test skips the `if` and falls through to `return true`, keeping every category. Every `matches` divergence is axis-wider, costing at most an empty row and never money. A previous revision claimed the guard lost money and built a criterion on it; that was wrong and is withdrawn.

One QA claim is also wrong and recorded so no future attempt chases it: BUG-2's suspected_cause and the coverage-gap list both say '_' reproduces BUG-2. It does not — this UNICODE_LIKE is a JS function treating only '%' and '?' as wildcards, so '_' is a literal. Executed: likePatternToRegex('X_') does not match 'CSharp', likePatternToRegex('_%') does match 'C_Sharp', and the axis and query agree on '_'. Escaping it would introduce a divergence where none exists.

Verified by execution: the served filterCategoriesByConditions, extracted verbatim from the module QA captured at the PR head, was run against the query evaluation reconstructed from compiler.ts and sqlite/index.ts over a fixture containing 'Café', 'C_Sharp' and '100% Off'. The proposed evaluation is byte-equal to the query on every value tested, including the eight on which the two already agreed.
work_order.approach:
Make the axis compute what the query computes, using the query's own primitives, instead of screening for the cases where it does not. Two edits; the second is the whole fix.

First, move the pattern language out of the SQLite platform layer into shared code, so there is exactly one implementation. Create packages/loot-core/src/shared/likePattern.ts exporting likePatternToRegex(pattern: string): RegExp, carrying REGEX_SPECIAL and the translation loop verbatim from unicodeLike.ts:5-31 — backslash escapes only '%', '?' and a literal backslash and consumes both characters, '%' → '.*', '?' → '.', everything else emitted with REGEX_SPECIAL applied, result new RegExp(regexStr, 'i'). Do NOT add underscore handling or escaping of the user's value; this function's semantics ARE the query's semantics. Have unicodeLike.ts import it instead of defining it, keeping its LRU cache, signature and guards exactly as they are — only pattern construction is delegated. Its existing 12-case test file is the guard that this is a faithful move and must pass unedited. shared/ is the right home rather than an export from platform/server: desktop-client may import @actual-app/core/shared/* (an existing export-map entry, already used by ManageRules.tsx:14) and may not import another platform's modules.

Second, rewrite ONE branch. `contains` becomes `likePatternToRegex(getNormalisedString('%' + condition.value + '%')).test(getNormalisedString(textValue))` — literally what UNICODE_LIKE(getNormalisedString(right), NORMALISE(left)) does on the query side, pattern folded and text folded in the same order. `doesNotContain` becomes the negation of that same expression; the query's $notlike carries an `OR left IS NULL` disjunct (compiler.ts:741-744) that never fires for a category name, so the negation is exact. This is a visible behaviour change on that operator — today `doesNotContain '%'` keeps 24 of 25 categories while the query keeps 0 — and it is called out in risks.

`matches` is NOT touched. Its divergences are all axis-wider and cannot lose money. Leave `condition.value.length <= 256` and the /i flag exactly as they are. This is a deliberate refusal to widen the diff past the defect, and it reverses a claim made in a previous revision of this order.

Nothing else changes. is/isNot/oneOf/notOneOf stay byte-identical — they compare the same category.id the query compares. isSupportedCategoryCondition, canNarrowAxisByConditions, narrowCategoriesByConditions, the identity-return guard, the conservative fallback, filterEmptyRows and both call sites stay untouched. The gate is not wrong: it asks whether the disjuncts are about the axis, which is still the right question; it was relying on an equality that did not hold. Once the equality holds by construction, the '%' disjunct in BUG-3 makes the axis return every category and the query every transaction. AC-13's negative control still passes for the same reason it passed on this head. The query side is not touched — it is the correct side; the axis is what is brought into line with it.

files.change: New module exporting `export function likePatternToRegex(pattern: string): RegExp`. Move REGEX_SPECIAL and the translation loop verbatim from packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/unicodeLike.ts:5-31, unchanged and in the same order: backslash escapes only '%', '?' and a literal backslash and consumes two characters; '%' becomes '.*'; '?' becomes '.'; every other character is emitted with REGEX_SPECIAL applied; result is `new RegExp(regexStr, 'i')`. Do NOT add underscore handling or wildcard escaping of the user's value — the semantics of this function are the query's semantics, and unicodeLike's own 12 tests pin them. Header comment stating this is the single definition of the LIKE pattern language and that anything which must agree with UNICODE_LIKE must go through it rather than reimplementing it.
files.why: The pattern language currently exists once, inside the SQLite platform layer, which is exactly why the report's row axis could not be made to agree with the query: the desktop app has no lawful way to reach it. shared/ is what makes 'agree by construction' possible rather than 'agree by careful duplication'.

files.change: Delete the local REGEX_SPECIAL and likePatternToRegex definitions (lines 3-31) and add `import { likePatternToRegex } from '#shared/likePattern';`. Keep the lru-cache instance, the exported unicodeLike signature, the `if (!pattern) return 0` and `if (!value) value = ''` guards and the cache lookup exactly as they are — only pattern construction is delegated. The file's existing test (unicodeLike.test.ts, 12 cases covering wildcards, '?', escaped wildcards, doubled backslash, unicode case folding and null handling) must pass with no edit to it; that suite is the proof this change is behaviour-preserving.
files.why: One implementation, so the axis cannot drift from the query later. This is a move, not a change: everything reading UNICODE_LIKE (index.ts:283, index.electron.ts:158, index.api.ts re-exporting the electron module) keeps identical behaviour, so every rule and every report is unaffected.

files.change: In evaluateCondition, replace the `contains` branch so it computes what the query computes, adding imports of getNormalisedString from '@actual-app/core/shared/normalisation' and likePatternToRegex from '@actual-app/core/shared/likePattern'. `contains` becomes: `return typeof condition.value === 'string' && likePatternToRegex(getNormalisedString('%' + condition.value + '%')).test(getNormalisedString(textValue));` — keep the existing typeof guard. `doesNotContain` becomes the negation of that same expression. Do NOT touch `matches` — leave `new RegExp(condition.value, 'i')` and its `condition.value.length <= 256` guard exactly as they are; a previous revision of this order claimed that guard loses money and was wrong, because the failed length test falls through to `return true` and keeps every category. Leave is/isNot/oneOf/notOneOf byte-identical, and leave isSupportedCategoryCondition, canNarrowAxisByConditions, narrowCategoriesByConditions, the conservative fallback and both call sites untouched. Comment each rewritten branch with the query-side line it mirrors (transaction-rules.ts:641-649 and compiler.ts:733-736 for `contains`, compiler.ts:741-744 for `doesNotContain`) so the pairing is checkable when either side changes.
files.why: This is the fix. Routing the axis through the query's own two primitives makes the two agree by construction, which is the only way the next operator cannot reopen the same hole.

cases: Pins the translation itself, since both the query and the report axis now depend on it: '%' becomes '.*', '?' becomes '.', a backslash escapes only '%', '?' and a literal backslash and consumes both characters, a lone backslash before anything else stays literal, regex metacharacters in the pattern ('.', '+', '(', '[', '$') are escaped and match literally, and the result is case-insensitive.

The exact values this ticket turns on: likePatternToRegex('%%%') matches every string — which is why `Category contains %` selects every category on the query side — and also matches the empty string.

Pins that '_' is NOT a wildcard in this language, contradicting QA's report: likePatternToRegex('X_') does NOT match 'CSharp' and likePatternToRegex('_%') DOES match 'C_Sharp'. '_' is a literal here, and no test may ever assert otherwise. Exists so a future implementer who reads QA's coverage-gap note does not 'fix' a character the query treats literally.
Escaped wildcards: likePatternToRegex('100\\%') matches '100%' and does not match '1000'.

BUG-2 REPRODUCER, fails on the PR head: field 'category', op 'contains', value '%' returns ALL fixture categories, not just those whose name contains a literal '%'. The query's pattern '%%%' matches every name, so the axis must agree and must not empty itself. Assert the returned ids explicitly so a future over-escaping fix — one treating '%' as an ordinary character — also fails here.
BUG-2, second wildcard: value '?' likewise returns all fixture categories. On the PR head it returns [] because no fixture name contains a literal '?'.

BUG-3 REPRODUCER, at the helper level and through the gate: conditionsOp 'or' with [category oneOf ['cat-rent','cat-electric'], category contains '%'] returns the FULL axis — all three fixture groups' categories — not just the oneOf set. Fails on the PR head, where canNarrowAxisByConditions returns true and the axis narrows to Bills while the query unions in a '%' arm matching everything.

Pins the ESCAPED form so the fix cannot over-escape into the opposite divergence: value '\\%' keeps only categories whose name literally contains '%' — add such a name to a local fixture — and drops the rest, because the query reads '\\%' as an escaped wildcard. Without this case a fix that escapes the user's wildcards would pass every other case here and reintroduce the money loss in the other direction.

Pins a value that merely EMBEDS a wildcard, the case AC-14 and AC-15 used to get wrong: value 'o%' keeps exactly the categories whose name matches '%o%%' — containing 'o' followed by anything — and drops the rest. It is NOT required to keep every category: on the query side 'o%' is an ordinary narrowing filter. Assert exact ids so neither an over-broad fix (keeps everything) nor an over-escaping fix (keeps only names containing the literal 'o%') passes.

DIACRITIC case, the divergence QA did not report: value 'cafe' keeps a fixture category named 'Café', because the query's NORMALISE strips the accent and the axis's toLowerCase() does not. Add the 'Café' fixture locally. Fails on the PR head, which returns []. Same for value 'e', which must keep 'Café'.

MUST STILL NARROW (AC-13), the ordinary substring case: value 'o' still returns only the categories whose name contains 'o', and value 'Bills' on field 'category_group' still returns exactly the group-bills categories. The fix must not turn every text condition into a no-op — a blanket 'never narrow text conditions' implementation fails here and in the next case.

doesNotContain is the negation of the same pattern, not of .includes: value '%' returns [] (the query matches every name, so nothing survives the negation) where the PR head returns every category, and value 'o' returns exactly the categories whose name does not contain 'o'.

matches is NOT changed by this fix, and these two cases pin that it must not be: value 'RE' still returns ['cat-rent'] via the axis's /i flag even though the query's case-sensitive REGEXP matches nothing, and a `matches` value longer than 256 characters still returns EVERY category. The second is the guard this order deliberately leaves alone — it falls through to `return true`, which is axis-wider and costs no money. A previous revision claimed this lost money and was wrong; these cases make that claim checkable rather than argued.

The category_group text path behaves identically, since textValue resolves to the group name: field 'category_group', op 'contains', value '%' returns every category whose group matches, and value 'Fun' still narrows to group-fun categories. The existing 'matches text operators against category group names' case must still pass unchanged.

BUG-2 MONEY, full pipeline with exact figures, using the serverRows seam the branch already has (vi.hoisted, feeding the #queries/aqlQuery mock). Conditions [category contains '%'], conditionsOp 'and', serverRows carrying spending in three categories (c-food -700, c-rent -300, c-cell -500). The query matches every category for this condition, so all three must be on the axis and totalDebts must be exactly -1500. On the PR head the axis is empty of real categories and totalDebts is 0.00. Assert totalDebts, not the axis alone — an axis assertion can be satisfied by a report that renders the rows and then zeroes them.

BUG-3 MONEY, same seam: conditionsOp 'or' with [category oneOf ['c-cell'], category contains '%'] and the same serverRows must total -1500 and carry c-food and c-rent on the axis. Fails on the PR head, where the total comes back as the Bills branch alone.

THE CLASS-LEVEL INVARIANT, the one that would have caught both bugs without anyone reasoning about LIKE semantics: for each (op, value) shape in a table — contains '%', '?', '\\%', '_', 'o%', 'cafe', doesNotContain '%', plus plain values that already worked — assert that EVERY category the stubbed query returned spending for has a row on the rendered axis. One-directional on purpose: 'Show empty rows' legitimately renders categories the query returned nothing for, so the reverse assertion would be wrong. The stub's rows and the axis are built independently, so this is a real differential rather than a restatement of the implementation, and it is the assertion to keep if a fifth operator is added.

REGRESSION GUARD (AC-1/AC-13), so the money cases cannot be satisfied by narrowing being switched off: 'and' with the Bills-only oneOf selection still yields exactly the Bills categories with no c-food and no c-rent, and 'or' over two oneOf conditions still narrows to their union. The Payee differential from T-8, as a second assertion in the same test: Split -> Payee with the filter still applied reports the same figure the unfiltered Category report did. Both sides run the same query, so any disagreement localises the loss to the category axis. This is the control that proves the money is still in the data.

Browser reproduction of BUG-3, mirroring QA's T-9: record the baseline, Unselect All and tick only the Bills group, add the second condition Filters -> Category -> contains '%', Apply, then flip 'all of' to 'any of'. Assert 'Food' still renders and the total still equals the baseline. Fails on the PR head, where the axis collapses to the Bills categories.

The second assertion is the one that matters: a fix that made every text condition a no-op would pass the money cases and fail this one.

EMBEDDED-WILDCARD case, added because AC-14 and AC-15 used to over-claim here: with 'all of' and `Category contains 'o%'`, assert that every category the report fetches spending for has a row and that categories whose names contain no 'o' at all do NOT appear as non-zero rows. Do NOT assert that this filter is unfiltered — on the data side 'o%' is an ordinary narrowing pattern, and a criterion demanding otherwise would fail a correct fix.

Guards so none of the cases can go vacuous on a generated budget: assert the baseline row set is non-empty and contains 'Food' before applying any filter. 'Food' is hard-coded in the demo budget (packages/loot-core/src/mocks/budget.ts:815) and is stable across runs even though the money is not.

acceptance.check: With a category selection applied and 'Show empty rows' enabled, the report renders rows for SELECTABLE categories only: no category or group that appears as a checkbox in the sidebar and is unchecked. The synthetic Uncategorized / Transfers / Off budget rows are not sidebar checkboxes and are unaffected.

The same holds for a selection narrower than a whole group - ticking a single category shows no other sidebar category and no other sidebar group, at 0.00 or otherwise. As in AC-1 the synthetic Uncategorized / Transfers / Off budget rows survive.
With no category condition set - the default state - the axis is unfiltered and every category still appears when 'Show empty rows' is on. The fix must not narrow the default report.
A category condition the filter cannot safely interpret leaves the axis unfiltered rather than dropping rows, preserving today's behaviour for complex conditions.
Category conditions addressed to a group (field 'category_group') narrow the axis to that group's categories, matching how the amounts are already filtered.

Every split whose axis comes from the category data is fixed - Category, Group, CategoryGroup and Interval - plus the Split=Category table view, which is rendered from groupedData rather than the Category list.

Type=Budgeted still produces correct amounts, and its axis is now narrowed by the same helper - the previously-phantom zero rows for unchecked categories disappear there too. This is the same defect category as the report's Type=Spent.
No regression in existing report behaviour: the current reports e2e suite and the reports unit suites still pass.

The synthetic Uncategorized / Transfers / Off budget block is unaffected by the narrowing: it survives a category selection, because categoryLists appends uncategorizedGroup itself after the narrowed data rather than filtering it.

A category group that is legitimately empty in an unfiltered report is not dropped. With no narrowing in play the helper must return the input unchanged, not rebuild the grouped array and delete the empty group.

With the operator set to 'any of', the categories rendered by the report are a superset of the categories each individual condition renders on its own. A transaction matching ANY disjunct is in the result set, so its category must have a row to render into.

With the operator set to 'any of' and a category condition combined with a non-category condition, the report's total is not the 'all of' total whenever the non-category condition alone matched spending the category condition excluded.

The fix is narrow, not a revert. Where the conditions combined with 'any of' are ALL addressed to the category axis - two category conditions, or a category and a category_group - the union of the disjuncts still narrows the axis to exactly that union and nothing more. A category condition whose value is an ordinary substring also still narrows.

A category filter whose operator is 'contains' and whose value IS the wildcard character '%' - the whole value, nothing else - leaves the report exactly as an unfiltered one: the same category rows render and TOTAL SPENDING is the same figure. '%' on its own compiles to a pattern matching every category name on the data side, so it must select every category. Reproduced by QA as BUG-2: the report rendered zero rows and 0.00 while the same filter on Split=Payee reported the full baseline. Verified by reading both the rendered rows and the total, not the total alone. SCOPE, which matters and which a previous version of this criterion got wrong: this holds for the bare wildcard only. A value that merely CONTAINS a wildcard - 'o%', 'Fo%', '% Off' - is an ordinary narrowing filter on the data side and is governed by AC-17, not by this criterion; it must not be expected to render every category.

With the operator set to 'any of' and two category conditions, one of which is a 'contains' whose whole value is '%' or '?', every category still renders - including the demo categories outside the selected group - and TOTAL SPENDING equals the unfiltered baseline. Reproduced by QA as BUG-3: the axis collapsed to the selected group and the spending outside it was fetched and silently dropped. As in AC-14 this is scoped to the bare wildcard value; a value that merely embeds one is governed by AC-17.

A category filter whose operator is 'contains' matches category names the way the data side matches them, including names that differ only by a diacritic: `contains 'cafe'` includes a category named 'Café', so the unfiltered report's spending for 'Café' is not dropped from the total. Reading it as a plain case-folded substring search drops that spending silently.

For every category filter the report can build - each supported operator, with values that are plain, a bare wildcard, an embedded wildcard, an escaped wildcard, a literal underscore, diacritic-bearing and case-mismatched - every category the report fetches spending for has a row in the table. This is the property BUG-2 and BUG-3 both violate, asserted against the fetched data rather than against a list of expected category ids, so a fifth operator or a future change to the filter's value handling cannot reintroduce it unnoticed. The property is ONE-DIRECTIONAL on purpose: 'Show empty rows' legitimately renders categories the query returned nothing for, so a category having no row is only a failure when the report fetched spending for it. In particular a value that merely embeds a wildcard - 'o%' - PASSES this criterion by keeping every category the data side matched for it, without being required to keep every category in the budget.

qa_script: Open the app, 'Try the demo', then /reports/custom (fresh Custom Report, Data Table view, summary on, Split=Category, Type=Payment).

BASELINE: record the rendered row names and TOTAL SPENDING. Guard: the row set must be non-empty and must contain 'Food', a hard-coded demo category. If it does not, the run proves nothing - say so rather than passing it.

BUG-2 / AC-14: Filters -> Category -> contains, type '%' into the value as the WHOLE value, Apply. ASSERT the rendered row names are unchanged from the baseline set and TOTAL SPENDING is unchanged from the baseline figure. A bare '%' matches every category name on the data side, so the filter is a no-op and the report must be indistinguishable from the unfiltered one. The PR head renders zero rows and 0.00 here.

CONTROL: Split -> Payee without touching the filter. ASSERT the figure equals the baseline. Both splits run the same query, so this proves the money is still in the data and that any loss is on the category axis.
Remove the filter (Filters -> the condition -> delete) and confirm the report returns to the baseline before the next case, so the two do not compound.

BUG-3 / AC-15: in the category sidebar click 'Unselect All' and tick only the 'Bills' group. Then add a SECOND condition: Filters -> Category -> contains, type '%' as the whole value, Apply. With two conditions present the operator toggle appears - flip it from 'all of' to 'any of'. ASSERT 'Food' still renders and TOTAL SPENDING equals the baseline. The PR head shows only the Bills categories and a smaller total.

AC-17, embedded wildcard: remove the second condition, then with 'all of' apply `Category contains o%`. ASSERT that every category the report fetched spending for has a row, and that categories whose names contain no 'o' do not carry non-zero spending. Do NOT expect this filter to be unfiltered - on the data side 'o%' narrows normally. Asserting that it renders every category would fail a correct fix.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, so neither money case can pass from narrowing being switched off wholesale: set the operator back to 'all of' with the Bills-only selection and 'Show empty rows' on. ASSERT every category outside Bills is ABSENT - the axis must still narrow for a selection that genuinely describes it.

SECOND NEGATIVE CONTROL, aimed at the over-correction: with 'all of', apply `Category contains o` (no wildcard). ASSERT the axis is still narrowed - the categories whose names contain 'o' render and the others do not. A fix that turned every text condition into a no-op would pass both money cases and fail this one.

If you want the differential, run the same script against origin/main on a second port. Read its rows as the target shape, not as a number to compare against: it is a second origin with its own demo budget, generated from a different Math.random draw.
risks: This change moves a function between packages in loot-core. If the move is not a pure relocation, every rule evaluation, every report and the desktop sync server change behaviour at once. unicodeLike.ts's 12 existing cases are the guard and must pass without being edited; the change is mechanical, but it is the riskiest line in the diff and deserves the most careful review.

`doesNotContain` changes behaviour visibly. `Category doesNotContain '%'` currently keeps every category that does not literally contain a percent sign; after this change it keeps none, because the data side treats '%' as a wildcard matching every name. The new behaviour is correct and matches the totals, but a user who typed '%' expecting a literal will see their rows disappear. Same fix as `contains`, called out because it is the one user-visible change beyond the bug being fixed.

Diacritic folding becomes newly correct on the axis for `contains`. `Category contains cafe` will now match 'Café' where before it did not. That is what the data side has always done - before this change the query returned Café's spending and the axis had no row for it - so this is a bug fix, but it is a behaviour change to anyone relying on the narrower reading.

The acceptance criteria deliberately contain no absolute money figure. The demo budget is regenerated with Math.random in a QA run (.sdlc/qa/playwright.config.mjs does not set userAgent 'playwright', so Platform.isPlaywright is false and createTestBudget draws from a different sequence each time), so AC-14 and AC-15 assert equality with a baseline read in the same run. This is the third attempt on issue #4 and the second on this defect class. The class is 'the row axis and the query disagree about which transactions exist' — BUG-1 was the field dimension, BUG-2 and BUG-3 are the operator-semantics dimension. AC-17 is written to be the check that would have caught both, and it is the thing to watch if this ticket ever comes back: if a future bug is a third instance of this class, the invariant itself is not being tested where it matters.

The filter UI offers many more fields and operators than the two this ticket touched (notes, payee, account, amount, date, tags). Only category and category_group conditions reach the axis helper at all, so the others cannot produce this defect — but that reasoning has now been load-bearing twice, and QA's Split=CategoryGroup/Interval coverage gap is still open.

alternatives_considered.approach: Extend canNarrowAxisByConditions to decline to narrow whenever any category condition uses `contains` or `doesNotContain` at all.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It silences both bugs by refusing to narrow, which regresses correct behaviour to avoid a defect: `Category contains Food` is a legitimate, well-defined filter that should narrow to Food and must keep doing so (AC-13's negative control). It also leaves the divergence in place — the axis would still be reading text operators in a different language from the query — so the next operator or the next change to the pattern language reintroduces the class. The gate answers 'is this condition about the axis'; the defect is 'do the two sides mean the same thing by it', which is a different question.

alternatives_considered.approach: Escape LIKE metacharacters in the value on the AXIS side only — treat '%' in the user's value as a literal character, so the axis reads it the way it reads it today.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It makes the two sides disagree in the opposite direction rather than removing the disagreement. The query reads '%' as 'match anything'; an escaping axis reads it as 'match a literal percent sign' and would narrow to only categories whose names contain '%'. Money would still be lost, and the bug would now need a second fix. This is why the shared likePatternToRegex is the deliverable and the escaping is not.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the underlying LIKE semantics inside unicodeLike.ts so that '%' in a value is escaped there too, changing the query's behaviour for rules as well as reports.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A product decision disguised as a bug fix: a rule the user wrote with '%' in the value has always matched as a pattern, in the rule editor's live preview as well as in reports, and changing that is a behaviour change to every rule in every budget. It is a different ticket with a different owner. This order takes the direction that cannot change what any existing rule means.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave the axis alone and drop the LIKE metacharacters from the value at the report's filter entry point, in FiltersMenu.tsx, so a wildcard-bearing value never reaches either side.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It moves the divergence rather than removing it — the rules path still reaches conditionsToAQL with the raw value, so rules and reports would disagree about what the same condition means — and it would silently edit what the user typed, which is worse than either side reading it literally.

alternatives_considered.approach: Also rewrite the `matches` branch to use new RegExp(value).test(textValue) with no /i flag and no length guard, as a previous revision of this order proposed.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Rejected on the evidence, not on taste. Executing the served function shows every `matches` divergence runs axis-WIDER: the /i flag matches strictly more than the query's case-sensitive REGEXP, and a value over 256 characters fails the length test, skips the `if`, and falls through to `return true`, keeping every category. An axis wider than the result set costs at most an empty row under 'Show empty rows' and never money — it is the opposite of BUG-2. Deleting the guard would also change matching behaviour for every rule-style report filter nobody reported as broken. The previous revision asserted the guard 'rejects the value for every category'; that is what made it look like a third money-losing instance, and it is false.

review.title: The two sibling reports that read contains/doesNotContain against a category-derived axis were not fixed, so both still diverge from the query in the money-losing direction that is the whole point of this ticket.
budget-analysis-spreadsheet.ts carries the same unfixed literal-substring reading of contains/doesNotContain, and unlike Sankey it feeds a per-month category list that the report then sums.

Routing the user's raw filter value into new RegExp with no length or wildcard cap introduces catastrophic backtracking on the render path — a budget with a few hundred categories makes the report hang.
review.detail:
Routing the user's raw filter value into new RegExp with no length or wildcard cap introduces catastrophic backtracking on the render path — a budget with a few hundred categories makes the report hang.

`packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/budgetDataQuery.ts:249`

Evidence: Before this change the axis used String.includes, which is linear in the name's length. Now a value like %%%%%Z becomes /.*.*.*.*.*Z/i, whose failure case is the classic exponential-backtracking shape. Measured on this machine against a realistic 34-character category name ('Emergency Fund Vacation Savings Plan'), per category evaluation:
    3 '%' ->   3.0 ms
    4 '%' ->  21.4 ms
    5 '%' -> 149.7 ms
    6 '%' -> 847.3 ms
That is one category. narrowCategoriesByConditions runs the predicate once per category per condition on every report render (custom-spreadsheet.ts:93, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:45), so 200 categories at 6 wildcards is roughly three minutes of blocked main thread. Two aggravating factors specific to this call site: unlike unicodeLike (which memoises the compiled RegExp in an LRU), the new code recompiles the pattern for every single category; and unlike matches, which the file's own comment at line 268 defends with a 256-character guard, contains has no bound at all. The user types the value into a text box, so the input is entirely untrusted.

Fix: Either compile the pattern once outside the per-category loop (removes the recompilation but not the backtracking), or bound the input: short-circuit values above the matches length threshold and values with more than a couple of wildcards. A memoised compile plus a wildcard cap closes both halves.

The new axis path recompiles the LIKE pattern once per category per condition, and unlike `matches` it applies no length guard - so a value like %%%%%%Z backtracks catastrophically on the render path. The asymmetry with the implementation this code was extracted from is the design point; the timing is pre-existing elsewhere and larger.

`packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/budgetDataQuery.ts:249`

Evidence: Running the exact production expression against a 36-character name ('Emergency Fund Vacation Savings Plan'): 3 wildcards 5.75ms, 4 -> 40.7ms, 5 -> 298ms, 6 -> 1885ms, per category. Recompilation is not the cost - 200 compiles of the same pattern total 0.56ms - it is pure backtracking, so memoising alone buys nothing. Two facts bound the severity: main's query side already runs this identical regex once per transaction row (measured 3442ms for FIVE rows at 6 wildcards), and main's axis `matches` branch already runs new RegExp(condition.value, 'i') (budgetDataQuery.ts:162 on main). This is a local-first app where the user types their own filter, so the input is not untrusted in the sense that matters.

Fix: Worth a follow-up ticket, not this diff: cap the wildcard count (or bound the value) inside likePatternToRegex so every LIKE-pattern consumer inherits the guard, and give the axis the same LRU memoisation unicodeLike already has. The work order's unknowns[1] already suspected loot-core's own rule evaluation deserved the same treatment.

`contains` on a category axis now means LIKE-pattern in the custom and grouped reports and literal substring in the budgeted Sankey and budget-analysis reports, so the same filter text gives different answers in four reports - but this is an inconsistency, not fetched money being dropped.

Evidence: sankey-spreadsheet.ts:459/:465 and budget-analysis-spreadsheet.ts:246/:251 both still read `name.toLowerCase().includes(value.toLowerCase())`. Neither site is a row-axis/query divergence, though: filterCategoryGroups has exactly one caller, :328 inside createBudgetSpreadsheet, whose data comes from `send('api/budget-month', { month: m })` - no conditions passed - and the comment at :425-428 says so explicitly ("Budget data is fetched unconditionally ... so we must apply category conditions manually in JS"). budget-analysis-spreadsheet.ts:339 sums `send('envelope-budget-month', { month })`, likewise unconditioned. In both, the JS filter is the only filter, so nothing fetched is discarded; the reports just answer the question differently. The new module header's claim to be the single definition makes the leftover copies more visible than they were.

Fix: Raise as a follow-up ticket to route both sites through likePatternToRegex, matching what budgetDataQuery.ts:246-265 now does. It is a real consistency bug and a fair thing to want fixed; it is not the money-losing defect class, and neither file is in this PR's diff.

errors: the plan reviewer rejected this revision: AC-14 states the rule 'A category filter whose operator is contains and whose value CONTAINS a SQL wildcard character - % or ? - leaves the report exactly as an unfiltered one', and AC-15 repeats the same generalization. Both are false for every value in the class they name except the bare wildcard character. The implementer cannot edit a criterion and QA holds the PR to it. — Scope AC-14 and AC-15 to the value BEING the wildcard character rather than containing one - e.g. "whose value is '%' (or '?')" - and for values that merely embed a wildcard, assert the AC-17 superset property (every category the report fetched spending for has a row) instead of equality with the unfiltered baseline. AC-14, AC-15 and AC-17 must be worded so that a value of 'o%' is a legitimate passing case, and all three checked together: they are the same claim in three places and the same edit has to land in each. tests[] already pins the correct behaviour and should be left alone - in particular "value '\\%' keeps only the categories whose name literally contains '%'" and "value '_' returns exactly the fixture categories whose name contains a literal underscore", which an implementer who read AC-14's broad sentence would contradict.
